plugin.name: Level editor
plugin.description: Game objects in the model: spawn points, enemies, triggers, hazards, sound zones, pickups, doors with keys, save points, fixed cameras, jump pads and teleporters – with their properties and actions – a level mode with only the level tools, and export as glTF plus a level file for game engines.

panel.title: Level
panel.placeHint: Choose what to place, then click in the 3D view.
panel.placingHint: Click to place · Shift places more · R turns · Esc stops
panel.name: Name (node in the glTF)
panel.volumeSize: Volume {size} – change it with the Scale tool.
panel.exportHint: The model as glTF, and the level file with the objects – their names are the nodes in the glTF.
panel.templatesHint: Engine templates: a script that builds the game objects in Godot, Unity or Unreal – next to the model’s GLB.
panel.navSummary: The player gets to {reached} of {cells} cells (green) – orange is floor nothing leads to.

tool.name: Place level object
tool.status: Choose a kind in the Level panel – a click selects a level object.
tool.statusPlacing: Place {kind}: click on a surface · Shift places more · R turns by 45° · Esc stops

warnings.noSpawn: The level has no spawn point.
warnings.sameName: {count} objects are called “{name}” – their glTF nodes cannot be told apart.
warnings.sameId: The id “{id}” is used twice – exporting gives the copy a new one.
warnings.missingTarget: “{name}” points at “{id}”, which is not there.
warnings.keyMissing: Door “{name}” needs the key “{key}”, but no pickup gives it.
warnings.noKey: Door “{name}” is locked, but has no key and nothing unlocks it.
warnings.noStartCamera: None of the fixed cameras is the first one.
warnings.enemyNeverComes: Enemy “{name}” waits for an action, but nothing lets it come.
warnings.unreachable: “{name}” cannot be reached from the start.
warnings.spawnNowhere: Spawn point “{name}” does not stand on a floor with room to walk.

script.object: Places a level object (spawn, enemy, waypoint, trigger, hazard, soundzone, pickup, door, savepoint, camera, jumppad, teleporter) with its properties and actions; returns its instance id.
script.objects: The level objects of the model: id, kind, name, instance id, properties and actions.
script.file: The level file as an object – what the export writes as JSON.
script.block: Adds a room, corridor or stairs to the blockout and builds it; returns the piece’s id.
script.blockEdit: Changes a blockout piece (null removes it) and builds the blockout again.
script.blockout: Builds the blockout again (after doors moved), optionally on another grid.
script.atmosphere: Sets the level’s atmosphere – daylight (0 … 1), fog and its colour and reach, shown while editing – and returns it.
script.generate: Generates a floor plan from a seed as the blockout – rooms, corridors and, when wanted, game objects; returns how many it made.
script.template: The engine template (godot, unity or unreal) of the level as text.
script.nav: Builds the walking grid from the spawn points and returns its cell size, how many cells there are and are reached, and what cannot be reached.

commands.playFirst: Level test run in first person

blockout.title: Blockout
blockout.empty: No rooms yet – choose Room and drag a rectangle in the 3D view.
blockout.refreshTitle: Builds the blockout again – after doors were moved or removed
blockout.statusFirst: {kind}: click or press where it starts
blockout.statusSecond: {kind}: click or release where it ends · Shift: corridor along y first · Esc stops

hints.room: Drag a rectangle on the grid. Rooms side by side get a wall between them – a level door in it cuts a doorway.
hints.corridor: Click its start and its end. Where it runs into a room, the room opens.
hints.stairs: Drag its rectangle the way it goes up. It climbs from the floor height by “Climbs”.

errors.unknownKind: Unknown blockout piece “{kind}” – room, corridor or stairs

play.title: Test run
play.startHint: Walk through the level as the player: doors, triggers, pickups, cameras and hazards work as in the game.
play.status: Test run: WASD walks, Space jumps, E uses, V changes the view, Esc stops
play.help: Click in the view to look with the mouse · WASD walk · Shift run · Space jump · E use · F torch · V view · Esc stop
play.helpLocked: Mouse looks · WASD walk · Shift run · Space jump · E use · F torch · V view · Esc frees the mouse
play.helpFixed: WASD walk along the camera · Shift run · Space jump · E use · F torch · V view · Esc stop

atmosphere.title: Light and atmosphere
atmosphere.hint: Less daylight makes the level dark – then only its lights and the player’s torch light it. The test run always shows light and atmosphere.

generate.title: Generate a floor plan
generate.objects: With game objects (start, lights, enemies, health, save point, goal)
generate.hint: Rooms of random size linked by corridors – every room reached, a few loops. The same seed gives the same plan.
generate.replace: Replace the blockout (and with game objects the level’s objects)?

sounds.title: Sounds
sounds.hint: Sound zones and the action Play sound play a sound by its name – a file of that name (without its extension, e.g. door-creak.ogg for door-creak). Names without a file play a stand-in in the test run.

guide.title: Guide
guide.intro: Step by step to a first playable level. Each step ticks itself off once the model shows it – you can do them in any order.

actions.message: Add a message to the trigger

blockout.title: Block out the rooms
blockout.text: Draw rooms by dragging a rectangle on the grid, corridors by clicking their start and end, stairs the way they go up. Floor height, room height and ceilings come from the Blockout panel. No time? Generate a floor plan from a seed.
blockout.done: The level has a blockout – change or remove pieces in the Blockout panel.

spawn.title: Place the player’s start
spawn.text: Click on a floor to place the spawn point; R turns it by 45° before the click. The arrow shows where the player looks.

enemies.title: Add enemies and their round
enemies.text: Place an enemy, then waypoints for its round. Give the waypoints the same path name and an order, and the enemy that path in the Level panel – in the test run it walks it, sees and follows the player.

logic.title: Make things happen
logic.text: A trigger is a box the player walks into. Select it and add actions in the Level panel: open a door, let enemies come, switch a light or the camera, show a message. Lock a door and let a pickup give its key.
logic.done: Something in the level sets off actions.

light.title: Light it
light.text: Place lights (all around or spots; colour, reach, flickering, shadows) and set the mood in the Level panel: less daylight, fog. “Show while editing” shows it in the view; the test run always does.
light.done: The level has lights or a mood of its own.

check.title: Check it
check.text: The checks list what a game engine would trip over; the walking grid shows in green where the player gets to from the start. Click a problem to select its object.
check.done: No problems, everything can be reached.

play.title: Play it
play.text: Walk through the level: WASD, mouse to look, Space jumps, E uses, F torch, V switches the view, Esc ends. Enemies walk, triggers go off, doors open.

export.title: Take it into a game engine
export.text: Export the model as glTF and the level file next to it – the game objects with their properties, actions and the walking grid. The Level panel has templates for Godot, Unity and Unreal that build them in the engine.
